# TASK 2: Mechanical & thermal strategy

All coordinates, dimensions and part data are read from `hardware/lib/board_spec.py` at generation time. Thermal values are estimates with every assumption listed next to its result.

## 1. Heat paths

| Path | Stack | Key numbers (from the spec) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) Top | SoC mould top -> 0.1 mm phase-change pad (e.g. Laird Tpcm 580) -- flush on SoC lid -> 25 x 25 x 10 mm heatsink (Al 6063-T5, black anodised) -> 5 V PWM fan (impinging, radial exhaust over the board) | SoC seated height 0.90 mm; tallest part allowed in the keep-out 0.60 mm (rule) / 0.55 mm (actual, 86 x 0402 passives around U1) -> air gap under the heatsink base >= 0.35 mm (0.30 mm by rule), 0.45 mm with the uncompressed TIM |
| (b) Bottom | EPAD 7.5 mm -> 7x7 vias 0.30/0.60 mm @ 1.0 mm (VIPPO) -> L2 GND plane + 14 x 14 mm exposed B.Cu spreader -> optional bottom gap pad / chassis | array extent 6.6 mm inside the 7.5 mm EPAD; fill: IPC-4761 Type VII (resin-filled + copper-capped, VIPPO) |

The heatsink sits flush on the SoC lid: nothing inside the 25 x 25 mm keep-out is taller than 0.55 mm, so the base clears every 0402 by >= 0.35 mm. Black anodising is not a guaranteed insulator -- the gap is the insulation, and the 4-point spring clamp keeps the base parallel to the board.

The 14 x 14 mm B.Cu spreader size is a TASK 2 assumption (`SPREADER_MM` in tools/gen_docs.py); it is not yet a constant in board_spec -- PENDING until the placer/router owns it.

### 1.1 Via-array thermal resistance

```text
barrel area  A = pi/4 * (d^2 - (d - 2t)^2) = pi/4 * (0.300^2 - 0.250^2) = 0.02160 mm^2
one via      R = L / (k * A) = 1.60e-3 m / (385 W/m.K * 0.02160e-6 m^2) = 192.4 K/W
array        R = 192.4 / 49 = 3.93 K/W   (plating t = 25 um, L = board thickness)
L1 -> L2 only (0.135 mm of the 1.60 mm): 0.33 K/W  (heat reaches the GND plane almost for free)
solid-copper-filled vias would give 1.20 K/W (resin fill k ~0.3-1 W/m.K adds nothing)
```

Constriction in the planes, voids under the EPAD and the resin fill are ignored, so treat 3.9 K/W as the via contribution only.

EPAD tile alignment (computed): 25 of 49 via pads fall fully inside one of the 2.1 mm EPAD tiles (2.7 mm pitch); the other 24 straddle the 0.6 mm inter-tile gaps. If the footprint copper is tiled (not one solid pad), either merge the F.Cu to a solid 7.5 mm pad (paste stays tiled) or move the array onto the tile pitch.

Reading: with only the via array and the board (no heatsink) the SoC would run roughly 42 K above ambient at the 2.0 W design point; the heatsink + fan cut that to ~17 K and the via array still carries about 54% of the heat. The temperature drop across the via array itself is only ~4.2 K. With theta-JC(top) at a pessimistic 20 K/W the fan-on R j-a becomes 10.1 K/W.

### 3.1 Heatsink and fan selection

| Choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- |
| Base = keep-out | 25 x 25 mm base covers the 25 x 25 mm keep-out exactly; everything under it is <= 0.55 mm |
| Height | 10 mm keeps the fan top low; the fan shadow is the fan footprint (up to 30 mm square, see section 6) |
| Pin fins | an impinging fan exhausts radially only through pin (or cross-cut) fins; plate fins would dump all flow along two sides |
| Fan | 25 x 25 x 10 mm or 30 x 30 x 7 mm, 5 V, 4-wire PWM, screwed to fin top; 5 V from VSYS through the high-side switch; typically 0.3-0.6 W for this size (check the fan datasheet) |
| Clamp | 4 x M2.5 spring-loaded screws through H1-H4 into a 30 x 30 mm X-bracket; plated holes tied to GND bond the heatsink to ground |
| Margin | theta-SA falls from ~30 to ~7 K/W with the fan (estimate; use the vendor theta-vs-airflow curve for the final part) |

## 6. Airflow

The fan blows down into the pin fins; air leaves the fin field radially at board level and sweeps the top copper. Rules applied: parts taller than half the heatsink height (5.0 mm) stay outside the fan shadow (largest fan option, +/-15.0 mm); heat sources should sit in the near exhaust (<= 15 mm from the keep-out edge) or far exhaust (<= 30 mm). Zones are geometric estimates, not CFD.

## 7. Fan control

J7 Intel 4-wire PWM fan header (1 GND, 2 +V, 3 TACH, 4 PWM). Intel 4-wire PWM fan spec: 25 kHz nominal (21-28 kHz), the PWM input is driven open-collector/open-drain against the fan's internal pull-up, an open or high input means full speed, tach is open-collector with 2 pulses per revolution.

| Function | Parts (netlist) | Signal path | Reset / fail-safe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PWM (open drain) | Q3 AO3400A; gate R86 100; pull-down R87 100k; optional pull-up R88 10k (DNP) | GPIO9 `FAN_PWM` -> J7.PWM `FAN_PWM_OD` | GPIO floats at reset -> R87 100k holds the FET off -> the fan's own pull-up reads 100 % duty |
| Fan power (high side) | Q4 AO3401A from `VSYS_5V`; gate pull-up R89 100k; driver Q5 AO3400A | GPIO11 `FAN_EN` | R90 10k pulls `FAN_EN` high -> driver on -> fan powered at reset; low = zero-RPM |
| Tach | pull-up R91 10k; series R92 1k | J7.TACH -> GPIO10 `FAN_TACH` | input; count falling edges in PCNT (2 pulses / rev) |

Fail-safe chain: any reset, brown-out, crash-induced watchdog reset or unflashed board leaves the fan GPIOs floating, so the fan is powered and at 100 %. Firmware only ever *reduces* cooling.

### 7.1 Suggested firmware fan curve (P4 internal temperature sensor, 3 K hysteresis)

| Die temperature | Fan duty | LEDC duty on GPIO9 (inverted by Q3) | GPIO11 FAN_EN |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| < 45 C (off again below 42 C) | 0 % | don't care | low (fan unpowered) |
| 45-55 C | 30 % | 70 % | high |
| 55-75 C | 30 -> 100 % (linear) | 70 -> 0 % | high |
| >= 75 C | 100 % | 0 % | high |
| sensor error / tach fault | 100 % | 0 % | high + raise alarm |

Starting values only -- retune once the thermal numbers in section 3 are measured. Update once per second, slew-limit the duty (~5 %/s) to avoid audible hunting, and treat a tach reading below ~300 RPM for 3 s while duty >= 30 % as a stalled fan (force 100 %, flag an error).

```c
// ESP-IDF sketch -- GPIO numbers generated from board_spec.GPIO_MAP
#define FAN_PWM_GPIO  9   // LEDC, 25 kHz; output inverted by the open-drain FET
#define FAN_TACH_GPIO 10  // PCNT, falling edges, glitch filter ~1 us
#define FAN_EN_GPIO   11  // high = fan powered (board default via pull-up)
temperature_sensor_handle_t ts;               // driver/temperature_sensor.h
temperature_sensor_config_t tcfg = TEMPERATURE_SENSOR_CONFIG_DEFAULT(20, 100);
temperature_sensor_install(&tcfg, &ts); temperature_sensor_enable(ts);
for (;;) {
    float t; int duty = 100;                  // fail-safe default
    if (temperature_sensor_get_celsius(ts, &t) == ESP_OK) duty = fan_curve(t);  // table above
    if (tach_stalled(duty)) duty = 100;
    gpio_set_level(FAN_EN_GPIO, duty > 0);
    ledc_set_duty(LEDC_LOW_SPEED_MODE, LEDC_CHANNEL_0, ((100 - duty) * LEDC_MAX) / 100);
    ledc_update_duty(LEDC_LOW_SPEED_MODE, LEDC_CHANNEL_0);
    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(1000));
}
```
